nodes.name: A saved change should be safe to continue.
nodes.text: ## A saved change should be safe to continue.

nodes.name: An editor needs room to experiment with copy, layout and…
nodes.text: An editor needs room to experiment with copy, layout and images. Saving that work should not silently change a public page that other people are already reading.

nodes.name: Grid keeps the editable page separate from its published…
nodes.text: Grid keeps the editable page separate from its published snapshot. A later draft remains private until an authorized manager explicitly publishes it again. Agents with Grid edit access save drafts too; that grant never carries publishing authority.

nodes.name: A page can refer to a background image, an uploaded font,…
nodes.text: A page can refer to a background image, an uploaded font, or media placed in a node. Those files matter as much as the text when deciding what will become public.

nodes.name: Publishing captures the saved page and the exact versions…
nodes.text: Publishing captures the saved page and the exact versions of the Grid assets it references, including an optional cover image and its description. Uploading a replacement later does not change what is public until the page is published again. Private Memory assets never become Grid content, because a Grid page can only refer to Grid assets.

nodes.name: Hidden nodes are still part of the published document.…
nodes.text: Hidden nodes are still part of the published document. Visibility is a layout setting, not a way to keep something confidential.

nodes.name: A content pool connects a public key to a Grid folder and…
nodes.text: A content pool connects a public key to a Grid folder and everything inside it. Only pages that were explicitly published into the pool appear in its listings. Moving a draft to another folder doesn’t change where its published version appears until it is published again.

nodes.name: Readers fetch published pages with a workspace API key. A…
nodes.text: Readers fetch published pages with a workspace API key. A public key can ship in a browser or mobile app because it can only read published content; a key that is invalid or revoked is rejected rather than treated as an anonymous reader.

nodes.name: Why the split matters for agents.
nodes.text: ## Why the split matters for agents.

nodes.name: Agents make the separation more important, not less. An…
nodes.text: Agents make the separation more important, not less. An agent can produce a reasonable draft of a page in seconds and revise it many times. That is exactly the kind of work that should happen in private, where mistakes cost nothing and a person can look at the result before anyone else does.

nodes.name: Keeping publication as a separate browser action for…
nodes.text: Keeping publication as a separate browser action for managers means an agent can be trusted with editing without also being trusted with the public face of a product. If you want an agent to help with a launch page, give it Grid edit access; the decision to make that page public stays with a person.

nodes.name: Withdrawal is a separate action too.
nodes.text: ## Withdrawal is a separate action too.

nodes.name: Unpublishing a page, disabling its pool or deleting the…
nodes.text: Unpublishing a page, disabling its pool or deleting the page withdraws its public URLs, including its assets. Every public read checks the current publication state before returning anything, so withdrawal takes effect immediately. It cannot erase copies a reader has already downloaded.

nodes.name: The public API, the `@nulldull/grid-core` library and the…
nodes.text: The public API, the `@nulldull/grid-core` library and the `@nulldull/grid-react` renderer follow the same saved document contract. Both packages are published on npm at 0.1.0 as early access releases. Custom node data only renders through components the consuming application deliberately registers, and the host application decides how to handle consent for external embeds.
